messages:
maria: heads-up: we're seeing sustained latency cliffs and some incorrect outputs on paged generation requests. Correlation looks strong with a KV cache reuse path that started shipping in the last runtime deploy. Errors include stale tokens and occasional cross-request leakage.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-234 created by maria (sev2) — channel: #incidents — pager on-call: kevin.
kevin: on it. summary of what I see from metrics: 95p latency doubled for seq>1024 workloads, mem usage on gpu-hosts spiked -> OOM recoveries, and request traces show mismatched KV sequences. Paging churn is high.
julia: logs show cases where a request re-uses a KV entry with a seq_offset that belongs to a prior request. Example trace: `kv_lookup(session=abc123, key=0x8f, seq_offset=427)` then later reused with `seq_offset=421` for a different session.
sam: customer impact? any live customers affected?
maria: yes — two customers reported garbled completions and one internal QA job saw duplicated token prefixes. Not universal but reproducible with long-context paged prompts.
oncall-sre: checklist: 1) isolate bad runtime build 2) stop rollout 3) mitigate traffic 4) handoff if needed.
kevin: doing a quick rollback to runtime v4.8.1 (pre-kv-reuse-change) to stop further exposure. Pushing a config hotfix to disable continuous-batching KV reuse heuristics (temp).
julia: pushing flag now: `KV_CACHE_REUSE_ENABLED=false` via fleet roll. Command: 
```bash
redwoodctl deploy-config --env prod --set KV_CACHE_REUSE_ENABLED=false
```
maria: also throttling paging batch sizes to reduce cache pressure: `MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=512` and `PAGING_WINDOW=2`. Applying canary first to 10% traffic.
kevin: canary applied to us-west-2, watching. If latencies drop and errors go away, we'll expand.
incident-bot: Canary started at 1888123600 — target 10% for 15m.
julia: noticed smaller request tail latencies already improving on canary nodes, error traces for stale offsets reduced from ~40/min to ~3/min.
sam: can we add a short-term mitigation for requests in flight? Something to scrub KV entries on context switch?
kevin: hotfix patch landed on canary to zero-out KV pointers on new-session boundary: 
```python
# quick guard: on session start
for slot in kv_slots:
    slot.seq_offset = -1
    slot.owner_session = None
```
Applied as part of canary build 4.8.2-hotfix.
maria: rolling to 50% now, monitoring for regressions and memory behavior. If OOMs persist we may need to reduce paging buffer sizes or fallback to non-paged generation for certain customers.
kevin: noticed one weird trace where reuse happened but seq_offset matched and still produced wrong tokens. looks like stale values in KV (value bytes not updated). suspect a race between writeback and session switch.
julia: adding additional metric: `kv_writeback_latency_ms` and a counter `kv_seq_mismatch` to track exact mismatch events.
oncall-sre: we've escalated to eng-runtime and eng-ml. pinging @eng-runtime-channel for deeper triage.
kevin: on-call handoff coming up in 40m. I'll brief the next oncall: summary, active mitigations (rollback + flags + batch throttles), canary status (50%, improving), customer list (cust-A, cust-B, internal-QA), postmortem owner: julia.
sam: do we have a list of affected requests to replay for a regression test?
julia: yes, captured 12 failing traces and a minimized repro harness. I'll upload to the test bucket and attach to the postmortem. repro notes included.
maria: customer communication: notifying engineering support to reach out to cust-A and cust-B with ETA and mitigation steps. Recommend advising temporary rate-limits and ask them to switch to non-paged mode if they depend on strict token correctness.
incident-bot: Update: at 1888123950 rollback fully expanded to prod (v4.8.1). Flags applied cluster-wide.
kevin: post-rollback metrics look good: 95p latency back to baseline, error traces down to noise. No new OOMs.
julia: still collecting kv_seq_mismatch counters — they dropped >90% after rollback+flags. We should keep enhanced telemetry for 24h.
maria: agreed. Julia will own postmortem and root cause. Action items:
- julia: RCA + postmortem (include repro and unit tests)
- kevin: follow-up fix for writeback race and integration tests for seq offsets
- sam: customer comms + support tickets
- oncall-sre: keep monitoring for 24h and escalate if counters rise
kevin: handoff to next oncall (alex) in 20m. alex you'll have the runbook and playbook in the incident doc.
oncall-sre: Please record any follow-ups here. If we see a recurrence, we will consider a deeper rollback of the continuous-batching feature set and schedule a patch release.
maria: thanks all — lowering to sev3 as impact is contained. Will update when postmortem ready.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-234 status changed to 'stabilized' at 1888124090.
kevin: leaving a short note for the next oncall: watch for any KV-related anomalies when traffic patterns spike (paging-heavy customers). Also check `kv_cache_len` and `kv_seq_mismatch` hourly for 24h.
julia: starting RCA writeup now, ETA 48h. I'll include a proposed long-term fix: stricter ownership model for KV slots + atomic writeback with per-slot epoch counters.
sam: thanks team — feel free to ping me if customer comms need escalation.
maria: closing channel for now, will re-open if we see new signals.
